disclaimer: Photographs illustrate possible signs, not a diagnosis or verified local detection. Disease photos depict symptoms, not insects; some comparisons intentionally show different diseases. Confirm clues and consult Extension advice before treatment.

clues.label: Eggs or groups of tiny bugs
Sticky residue or clusters of soft insects
Tiny yellow or pale speckles on leaves
Fine silk webbing on leaf undersides
White powder coating on a leaf
Blocky yellow patches between leaf veins
Brown or gray leaf spots with edges or rings
Chewed corn kernels near the silk end
Damage to squash or cucumber blossoms

pests.name: Squash vine borer
pests.diagnostic: Check the stem base for tan frass or tunneling. Wilting alone may be drought or root trouble.
pests.lookalike: Drought stress, bacterial wilt and root injury can also make squash wilt.

pest.author: Melissa McMasters
pest.alt: Orange-and-black adult squash vine borer moth on vegetation
pest.caption: Adult moth; look for the orange abdomen and clearwing-moth shape.

damage.author: Massiv99
damage.alt: Cut-open zucchini stem revealing pale squash vine borer larva and tunnel
damage.caption: Inside-stem evidence: a pale larva and damaged stem tissues, not a wilt diagnosis by itself.

pests.name: Squash bug
pests.diagnostic: Look on lower leaf surfaces and near stems for coppery eggs or clusters of gray nymphs; feeding can cause localized collapse.
pests.lookalike: Squash vine borer can also cause wilting; look for frass at the stem rather than bug clusters.

pest.author: Downtowngal
pest.alt: Brown adult squash bug seen from above
pest.caption: Adult squash bug; note the flattened brown body.

damage.file: Anasa nymphs on stem of a squash plant in garden.jpg
damage.author: Mordekai99
damage.alt: Cluster of young squash bug nymphs on zucchini stem
damage.caption: Early field clue: young squash bug nymphs, not a photograph of damaged tissue.

pests.name: Flea beetles
pests.diagnostic: Small jumping beetles and numerous pinholes on tender leaves are a characteristic combination.
pests.lookalike: Caterpillars also make holes, often larger and more irregular; holes alone cannot identify the feeder.

pest.author: Sangeetha N shet
pest.alt: Small dark flea beetle macro photograph
pest.caption: Illustrative flea beetle; this photograph need not be the species on your crop.

damage.author: Schlaghecken Josef
damage.alt: Beet leaf with tiny shot-hole injury from a Chaetocnema flea beetle
damage.caption: Illustrative shot-hole feeding on beet leaves; this is not a Michigan crop-specific species confirmation.

pests.name: Cabbageworms and loopers
pests.diagnostic: Turn leaves over for caterpillars, dark frass and irregular chewing; photos show imported cabbageworm, one of several possible caterpillars.
pests.lookalike: Flea beetles make smaller shot-holes. Slugs may cause ragged holes and leave slime.

pest.author: Boyana.kjfg
pest.alt: Green imported cabbageworm caterpillar on cabbage
pest.caption: Imported cabbageworm, one of the caterpillars covered in this watch.

damage.file: Brokkoli Cabbage white, Fraßschaden des Kleinen Kohlweißlings. Whitney Cranshaw, Colorado State University, Bugwood.org.jpg
damage.author: Whitney Cranshaw, Colorado State University, Bugwood.org
damage.alt: Broccoli leaves with large caterpillar feeding holes
damage.caption: Chewed broccoli leaves attributed by the source to imported cabbageworm.

pests.name: Tomato hornworm
pests.diagnostic: Look high on tomatoes for missing leaflets, dark droppings and a large green caterpillar; tobacco hornworms can cause very similar injury.
pests.lookalike: Tobacco hornworm is a close lookalike and also feeds on tomatoes. Do not diagnose species from damaged leaves alone.

pest.author: Geo Lightspeed7
pest.alt: Green tomato hornworm caterpillar eating a tomato plant
pest.caption: Large green hornworm in a home tomato garden.

damage.author: Ljessee123
damage.alt: Hornworm on partly defoliated tomato plant
damage.caption: Hornworm feeding and associated missing tomato foliage; assess the full plant before acting.

pests.name: Colorado potato beetle
pests.diagnostic: Inspect potatoes and eggplants for striped adults, orange eggs and reddish larvae that chew foliage.
pests.lookalike: Three-lined potato beetles and other leaf feeders may be confused at a glance; confirm body markings.

pest.file: Imago of Colorado potato beetle on leaf.jpg
pest.author: Adámozphoto
pest.alt: Yellow striped adult Colorado potato beetle on a leaf
pest.caption: Adult beetle with distinctive dark stripes.

damage.author: Tavo Romann
damage.alt: Colorado potato beetle larvae actively chewing potato leaves
damage.caption: Larvae feeding on potato foliage; look for irregular losses along leaf edges.

pests.name: Japanese beetle
pests.diagnostic: Check for metallic-green adults with copper-brown wing covers near lacy leaf skeletonization. Similar injury can have other causes.
pests.lookalike: Other chewing insects can skeletonize leaves; verify the adult before choosing a response.

pest.author: Ryan Hodnett
pest.alt: Metallic green Japanese beetle with copper wing covers
pest.caption: Adult Japanese beetle; photograph is not a Michigan sighting.

damage.file: Japanese beetle damage to a rose leaf.JPG
damage.author: SB_Johnny
damage.alt: Rose leaf with lacy skeletonized feeding injury attributed to Japanese beetles
damage.caption: Rose leaf skeletonization; photo does not prove beetles are currently present.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.diagnostic: Look for clusters of small, soft-bodied insects, often at tender shoot tips or under leaves. Sticky honeydew and curled growth can support the identification.
pests.lookalike: Heat, herbicide drift and some diseases can curl leaves. Ladybug larvae and lacewing larvae are beneficial predators; do not treat them as aphids.
pests.whatToCheck: Turn over a new leaf and inspect the shoot tip with a hand lens. Check for living aphids and beneficial predators before choosing any control.

pest.author: Sanjay Acharya
pest.alt: Close-up of cabbage aphid colony on kale
pest.caption: Aphids photographed on kale; illustrative of soft-bodied colonies on leaf surfaces.

damage.author: Jochen Kreiselmaier, DLR Rheinpfalz
damage.alt: Chinese cabbage foliage yellowed and distorted by aphid feeding
damage.caption: Aphid-associated yellowing of Chinese cabbage; appearance varies by crop and aphid species.

pests.name: Striped and spotted cucumber beetles
pests.diagnostic: Look for small yellow beetles with black spots or three dark stripes. Check cucumber seedlings and squash blossoms for fresh chewing.
pests.lookalike: Lady beetles and some harmless leaf beetles can appear similar. Wilting alone is not evidence of bacterial wilt or beetle transmission.
pests.whatToCheck: Look directly for striped or spotted beetles at flowers and tender leaves, then compare body patterns. Damage without a beetle cannot establish the culprit.

pest.file: Spotted Cucumber Beetle - Diabrotica undecimpunctata, Prince William Forest Park, Triangle, Virginia.jpg
pest.author: Judy Gallagher
pest.alt: Spotted cucumber beetle with yellow-green wing covers and black spots
pest.caption: Spotted cucumber beetle; striped cucumber beetles have a different wing pattern.

damage.author: Rob Mitchell, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
damage.alt: Cucumber beetle feeding damage on winter squash blossoms
damage.caption: Cucumber beetle injury in winter squash blossoms; not every torn blossom indicates this insect.

pests.name: Twospotted spider mites
pests.diagnostic: Early injury looks like pale stippling or bronzing, often starting on dry, dusty leaves. Dense infestations may leave fine webbing underneath.
pests.lookalike: Thrips, leafhoppers, nutrient stress and disease can create pale speckles. Webbing alone can come from spiders rather than spider mites.
pests.whatToCheck: Use a hand lens on the underside of a stippled leaf for tiny moving mites and eggs; inspect several leaves before judging whether intervention is warranted.

pest.author: Claudio Labita
pest.alt: Twospotted spider mites photographed on the underside of a bean leaf
pest.caption: Twospotted mites on bean foliage; tiny enough to require magnification.

damage.file: Stokboon bonenspintmijt Phaseolus vulgaris with Tetranychus urticae.jpg
damage.author: Rasbak
damage.caption: Bean leaf damage associated with twospotted mites; feeding injury is not species-specific.

pests.name: Cucurbit powdery mildew
pests.diagnostic: Powdery mildew produces whitish, powder-like colonies on leaves, typically becoming more obvious as growth matures.
pests.lookalike: Some squash varieties have naturally silvery leaf markings. Dust or pesticide residue can also look white; confirm raised, spreading fungal growth rather than pattern alone.
pests.whatToCheck: Look for new powdery patches on both leaf surfaces and check whether the white areas expand over days. Natural variegation is part of the leaf pattern.

pest.author: Schlaghecken Josef
pest.alt: White powdery mildew colonies on a pumpkin leaf
pest.caption: Close view of a pumpkin leaf with powdery mildew; this is a disease, not an insect.

damage.author: Schlaghecken Josef
damage.alt: Pumpkin foliage displaying powdery mildew over multiple leaves
damage.caption: Wider plant context for powdery mildew on cucurbit foliage.

pests.name: Tomato leaf spots
pests.diagnostic: Look for spotted older leaves; early blight may show concentric rings, while Septoria often creates smaller spots with pale centers.
pests.lookalike: Early blight and Septoria are DIFFERENT diseases. Bacterial spots, chemical injury, nutrient problems and late blight can resemble them; these photos cannot diagnose the causal organism.
pests.whatToCheck: Inspect spot shape, ring patterns, affected leaf age and recent moisture. Compare with Michigan Extension guidance before diagnosing; seek expert confirmation when symptoms are ambiguous.

pest.author: Dwight Sipler
pest.alt: Tomato leaves with larger brown lesions attributed to early blight
pest.caption: Example of early blight symptoms on tomato leaves, not a universal tomato leaf spot.

damage.author: Wolan268
damage.alt: Tomato leaf bearing multiple Septoria leaf spot lesions
damage.caption: Different cause: Septoria leaf spot on tomato, shown intentionally for comparison with early blight.

pests.name: Cucurbit downy mildew
pests.diagnostic: Angular yellow areas bounded by leaf veins may turn brown; disease progression often follows periods favorable to leaf wetness.
pests.lookalike: Powdery mildew usually has an obvious white, powdery coating. Nutrient problems, other leaf spots and drought stress can also cause yellow leaves.
pests.whatToCheck: Look for vein-bounded yellow patches and, when conditions are humid, gray-purple sporulation on the underside. Symptoms do not establish active local disease reports.

pest.file: Downy mildew on leaves of Cucumis sativus.jpg
pest.author: Wee Hong
pest.alt: Cucumber leaf with angular yellow patches from downy mildew
pest.caption: Close-up of downy mildew symptoms on cucumber foliage.

damage.author: Jerzy Opioła
damage.alt: Cucumber leaf showing symptoms attributed to Pseudoperonospora cubensis
damage.caption: A second photographic example of cucurbit downy mildew on cucumber.

pests.name: Slugs
pests.diagnostic: Irregular, smooth-edged holes and a silvery slime trail are useful clues, especially during damp nights or mornings.
pests.lookalike: Caterpillars, earwigs and other chewing pests can make similar holes. A hole without a slug or slime trail is inconclusive.
pests.whatToCheck: Check under boards, pots and damp debris at dusk or early morning. Look for an actual slug or a fresh slime trail on the crop.

pest.author: Theactivistuk
pest.alt: Garden slug moving across a surface
pest.caption: Garden slug, a mollusk rather than an insect.

damage.author: Dialectum
damage.alt: Slug actively feeding on leafy vegetables
damage.caption: Visible slug feeding on vegetables; this is direct field evidence, not an outbreak forecast.

pests.name: Corn earworm
pests.diagnostic: On sweet corn, inspect the silk end of ears for a caterpillar, frass and chewed kernels. Similar larvae may also damage tomatoes.
pests.lookalike: Bird feeding, other caterpillars and physical ear injury can resemble earworm damage. Adult moth photographs alone do not establish local egg laying.
pests.whatToCheck: Open an affected ear at the silk end and look for a larva and frass. Do not infer current trap pressure from historical photographs.

pest.author: Gregbaker
pest.alt: Corn earworm larva feeding on a corn cob
pest.caption: Corn earworm larva photographed on an ear of corn.

damage.file: Green caterpillar on ear of corn.jpg
damage.author: Sarah Zukoff
damage.alt: Green corn earworm among corn silk and kernels
damage.caption: Another corn-earworm feeding example at the ear tip; feeding damage can vary.
